title: Command Line Sandbox
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: A simulated Linux shell over the chapter's station file system, paired with a live file tree that highlights the working directory, a seven-task checklist, and an rm that really deletes so the consequence can be experienced safely.

learningObjectives: Execute shell commands to navigate a Linux file system and inspect its contents.
Read a permission block character by character and say what each position means.
Diagnose a missing execute bit as the reason a script will not run, and fix it with chmod.
State what rm does and why there is no way to undo it.
prerequisites: Chapter 12: the file system, shell commands and file permissions

keyQuestions: How do you find out where you are in the file system?
Why does your Python script refuse to run even though the file is clearly there?
What does each of the ten characters in -rw-r--r-- mean?
What happens to a file after rm, and how would you get it back?
commonMisconceptions: A file that exists and is readable can always be run.
rm asks for confirmation, or puts the file somewhere recoverable.
Permissions are a security feature that does not affect ordinary work.
cd tells you where you are.
assessmentOpportunities: Completes all seven guided tasks unaided and records the commands used.
Explains the ls -l output for /dev/i2c-1 in terms of the i2c group.
Describes what would have been lost had the deletion been on a real station.
